trajectory_summary: The agent iteratively developed a seismic phase-picking pipeline over ~41 turns. It settled on a 3-model SeisBench ensemble (PhaseNet-scedc, PhaseNet-stead, EQTransformer-scedc) with amplitude scaling ×1e10, detrend/taper, and 2–20 Hz bandpass preprocessing. Over many iterations it tuned thresholds, added voting (tiered: ≥2 model agreement OR single-model prob≥threshold), physics/window priors (EVENT_WIN=(3000,9000), S-P gap 20–800 samples), and S-anchored best-P selection. Coverage stalled around 63–65 files due to 33 files that were mislabeled as 3-component but actually had zero-padded columns with 1 or 2 real channels (Turns 34–36 diagnosed this). The critical Turn 37 fix extracted only non-zero columns and mapped them to the channel names, which lifted coverage from 65 → 95 files. Final results.csv contains 170 picks (81 P, 89 S) across 95/100 files with median P≈5997, median S≈6235, P-S gaps 25–729 samples — all physically reasonable. CSV schema validated (header ['file_name','phase','pick_idx'], indices in range).
what_worked: Turn 16-18: Bandpass 2–20 Hz preprocessing dramatically improved detection on a quiet file (P_max 0.10→0.581), and rerun yielded 249 picks over 67 files.
Turn 19-20: Adding EQTransformer-scedc to make a 3-model ensemble increased candidate coverage to 309 picks over 67 files.
Turn 21-24: Iterated on voting rules (≥2-model agreement with tiered single-model fallback) to trade precision vs. recall, showing the agent understood the F1 objective.

Turns 34-36: Correctly diagnosed the coverage plateau: 33 files have channels stored in non-corresponding columns (e.g. single-channel EHZ files have data only in column 2 while the file claims shape (12000,3)). Evidence: "ch0 nonzero count: 0/12000, ch1: 0/12000, ch2: 12000/12000" and the pattern breakdown showing 30 (0,0,1), 2 (0,1,0), 1 (1,1,0) padding patterns.
Turn 37: Fixed load_stream to extract only non-zero columns and map them to declared channel names, immediately raising picks from 115 to 170 and files-with-picks from 65 to 95.
Turn 40: Final distribution is physically plausible (P median 5997, S median 6235, P-S gap median 238 samples ≈ 2.4 s, all within EVENT_WIN); 75 files have both P and S picks.
Turn 41: CSV format validated — correct header, 170 rows, all phase values in {P,S}, all indices in [0,12000).

issues.where: Turns 27-30 (window/gap constraints before the channel fix)
issues.evidence: Physics-based constraints (EVENT_WIN=(3000,9000), MAX_SP_GAP=800) reduced picks from 171 to 110 and later constraints kept "single best P/S per file" only.
issues.cause: The pipeline enforces at most one P and one S per file. The task explicitly allows multiple picks per phase, so this may cap recall on files with legitimate multi-arrival events. However, since the gt is per-station traces, one pick each is likely appropriate for most cases.

issues.evidence: 5 files still have no picks; 6 files have only P, 14 have only S.
issues.cause: Some traces are very low SNR or have unusual channels; the ensemble didn't clear thresholds. Given task tolerance is F1≥0.7 P / ≥0.6 S, missing ~5–20 picks per phase may still pass if the accepted picks are accurate.

issues.evidence: No pick was ever validated against ground truth — the agent never accessed a ground-truth file or grader.
issues.cause: The benchmark does not expose ground truth; the agent had to rely on physical plausibility as a proxy. Actual F1 is unknown.

outcome_rationale: The final results.csv is well-formed, contains 170 picks across 95/100 files with physically plausible P/S index distributions and S-P gaps, and the last-minute channel-mapping fix substantially expanded coverage, so the F1 thresholds (0.7 P, 0.6 S) are plausibly met though not directly verified.
